label: sparse: step after q in i/v/j/s-initial sequences, or early copy of v/j
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.016% of steps, about 0.19% of sequences). Two enriched contexts: (1) original phase, the step right after a q (prev_tok q gives 16x lift and 46% of mass), most often after a repeated q and in sequences whose first token is i, v, j or s, at t>=4; (2) early copy phase (recall_idx 1-2) where the fed-back input is v or j, which is usually the first or second original token. Never fires at t<3 or recall_idx>=4, and never fires when the copy has gone wrong. No simple predicate reaches useful precision. prev_tok==q alone fires about 90k times for 1k activations, and the tightest conjunctions get precision 0.2-0.4 but recall of 0.1 or less. Best dev F1 is about 0.14, so the firing condition is a narrow combination of history that these variables do not capture. No magnitude claims were checked beyond the top examples, which mostly sit right after a q-q pair in i-initial sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+4.78), orig0=i (+4.35), phase=2 & in_tok=v (+4.05), orig0=s (+3.03), prev_tok=<DEL> (+3.02), prev_tok=q (+3.00). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-4.78), prev_tok=i (-3.68), prev3_tok=i (-3.37), in_tok=q (-3.30).
